query_text: Schliemann’s treatment of “Priam’s Treasure” raises a serious cultural heritage issue. He presented the gold objects as one dramatic discovery connected to King Priam, although David Traill argues that the collection included items found at different times (Traill, “Priam’s Treasure” 17–18). The objects belonged to Troy II and were about a thousand years too early for the usual date of the Trojan War
